chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, he narrated from one who narrated to him from Abu Sa'id al-Mad'ini, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I teach you something you should say in the Salat of Ja'far?' I said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'When you are in the final prostration of the four rak'at, say, after you have finished your tasbih (glorification):'

Glory be to He who wore honor and dignity, glory be to He who girded Himself with glory and honored with it, glory be to Him to whom glorification is due, glory be to He whose knowledge encompasses all things, glory be to the Possessor of bounty and blessings, glory be to the Possessor of power and command.
O God, I ask You by the knots of honor from Your Throne, and the utmost of mercy from Your Book, and Your Greatest Name, and Your perfect words which were completed in truth and justice,
Send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and do for me so-and-so.'

key_terms.صَلَاةُ جَعْفَرٍ: Salat of Ja'far (a specific type of prayer)
key_terms.مَعَاقِدُ الْعِزِّ: Knots of honor (referring to the Throne)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific dua to recite in the final prostration of Salat al-Ja'far?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith details the specific supplication for the final prostration of Salat al-Ja'far, a highly recommended prayer often recited for specific needs. The text highlights the theological concept of 'Ma'qid al-'izz' (the seat of honor) on the Throne, linking divine majesty with mercy, and concludes with the invocation of the 'Ism al-A'zam' (Greatest Name) to secure the fulfillment of personal petitions.
